assertions.text: Table has at least one column name ending with '?' (e.g. 'Discount?' or 'Expected?')
assertions.evidence: Discount? column in header: 'Scenario | Customer tier | Discount?'

assertions.text: Table has exactly 3 data rows (GOLD, SILVER, BRONZE)
assertions.evidence: Three data rows: 'Gold customer | GOLD | 20', 'Silver customer | SILVER | 10', 'Bronze customer | BRONZE | 0'

assertions.text: Test method body contains only one assertEquals (or equivalent assertion) — not three
assertions.evidence: Method body contains single line: 'assertEquals(discount, discountService.calculate(customerTier, 100));'

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Method body contains only 'assertEquals(discount, discountService.calculate(customerTier, 100));' with no conditional logic

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column in table header is 'Scenario'

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case
assertions.evidence: Method name 'calculatesDiscountByCustomerTier' converts to 'Calculates Discount By Customer Tier', a clear descriptive title

assertions.text: If @Description is present, it provides context beyond what the table rows already express
assertions.evidence: @Description("Order value is always 100.") provides fixed parameter context not visible in table columns. Response notes: 'The order value (100) is fixed across all rows, so I'll note it in @Description rather than repeat it as a column'

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order
assertions.evidence: Annotations appear as @Description followed by @TableTest (correct order with @DisplayName absent)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description text "Order value is always 100." is short and fits on a single line, so text block is not required
